LOCATION HELP

Turn on Live Location

Atlas can follow your position only after you choose to allow location access. Your precise coordinates stay in your browser.

Installing Atlas does not bypass your phone or browser location permission. Live Location runs only while Atlas is open and stops when you choose Stop, Reset, or leave the page.

Help & About

Checking this device…

Install the EPR Atlas

Loading the best instructions for this device.

Installing adds the Atlas to your Home Screen or app list for faster access. The website remains the same public EPR Atlas and updates can be delivered through the web app.

Explore

  • Tap a parcel, facility, well, or infrastructure symbol for details.
  • Use Layers to turn categories and the Water Story on or off.
  • Use Legend to see what symbols and evidence treatments mean.
  • Use Find & nearby to search by name/address/APN, scan around the map center, or choose What's here? and tap any spot on the map.
  • Use Share this asset in a record card to create a direct link back to that exact public record.
  • Tap Reset to return to the Atlas starting view.
  • The location button starts Live Location. Your blue dot updates as your phone reports new positions. Drag the map to explore without stopping the dot; tap the location button or Recenter to follow again.
  • The light-blue halo shows your phone's reported GPS accuracy. Larger circles mean less precise readings.
  • If location is unavailable, Atlas explains whether permission, GPS availability, or a timeout is the issue and provides installation/help guidance.

How to read the map

Labels such as approximate, orientation, supported, or not survey-grade are intentional evidence qualifiers. They are not interchangeable with surveyed boundaries or exact engineering locations.

Find, share & explore nearby

Search public records, explore mapped assets around the map center or your device, share a direct record link, or use What's here? to inspect a point on the map.

About the EPR Atlas

The EPR Atlas is a public-records map created by Enid Public Record to help residents explore public property, facilities, infrastructure, and major public investments associated with Enid, Oklahoma.

Enid Public Record is independent and is not an official City of Enid website.

Legal & evidence notice

Informational use. The Atlas is compiled from public records and other documented sources for reporting and public-information purposes. It is not a survey, title opinion, legal description, engineering plan, or substitute for an official record.

Location and boundaries. Parcel geometry, infrastructure alignments, facility points, wellfield locators, and other mapped features may be generalized or approximate where the evidence does not support survey-grade precision. Qualifiers shown in the Atlas are part of the record.

Changes and verification. Ownership, condition, status, and public records can change. For a legal, financial, construction, or property decision, verify the underlying official record with the responsible public agency.

Privacy. Live Location starts only after you tap the location control or choose Use my location. Your coordinates stay in your browser and are not sent to EPR analytics or placed in shared URLs. Tracking stops when you choose Stop, tap Reset, or leave the Atlas.

Copyright. © 2026 Enid Public Record. Original reporting, text, graphics, cartographic presentation, and EPR branding are protected. Underlying public records and third-party basemap material remain subject to their own applicable rights and terms.

Acquisition years
Year filters are true visibility filters in v14.9: turn a year off and that year's acquisitions disappear. Owner remains encoded by the polygon outline.
Water Story
DEQ Active/Inactive is regulatory component status, not proof a well is pumping today. Monitoring wells are non-production. Nine confirmed monitoring/observation records remain location-held.
Master control selects or clears every Water Story layer. Pipelines can be hidden independently from Kaw Project sites. A partial selection is shown with the master checkbox in an indeterminate state. Verified mapped records are displayed. Ames Plant is a documented City of Enid water facility.
